Q: Tasks.json - detecting a Windows errorlevel return value from a shell task? A:

I just noticed that it seems the terminal window automatically picks up the errorlevel emitted from the executable.

The terminal process "C:\...\powershell.exe -Command & 'C:\...\FOO.exe' terminated with exit code: 1.

And indeed, if I create a composit sequence-based (not parallel) task using dependsOn, it does not execute the second task if it sees the first error.

This seems to work well, the only thing now: I need a way to silence/satisfy this input question when running it.

Continue without scanning the task output

I assume that's because I have no problemMatcher?

EDIT: never mind, seems I can just place an empty problemMatcher in the task. "problemMatcher": []

Q: What is the practical need for right outer join in SQL if left outer join can achieve the same result? A:

In many cases it comes down to readability and maintenance, especially if you have a collection of similar queries or many that use the same core query.

  • If you do not use SELECT * and you do include an ORDER BY clause then output should not be any different if you properly rewrite the query to replace a RIGHT OUTER JOIN with a left one.

Rewriting a common query just to avoid a RIGHT OUTER JOIN can complicate maintenance and QA checks later as reviewers will first consider rewriting the query to match the common implementation, or because it doesn't match the standard it may diverge from the common intent as the common implementation is refactored as your product matures.

While there is no functional advantage of choosing to base a simple query around a RIGHT OUTER JOIN over LEFT OUTER JOIN on it's own, if your query requires many joins, then you may find the query easier to think about and structure using a RIGHT OUTER JOIN.

The advantage therefore is situational in that for a given query, to join in an additional table and include all of it's rows, not just those that match, RIGHT OUTER JOIN is the tool to use.

A similar question could be asked about the order of the fields in the ON clause of the join statement. By convention many people prefer the left table reference on the left of the equality, and the right table on the right... You could try to maintain this convention but especially when a query is refactored to reverse the left and right tables (perhaps to avoid a RIGHT OUTER JOIN?) you can very easily end up with the ON clause reversed, and the outcome would be no different.

Q: Can a userscript delete cookies from a given domain? A:

Since around 2025 all major browsers support the CookieStore-API, which allows for:

cookieStore.delete('NAME_OF_COOKIE'));

See: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CookieStore

Q: Python: Can't display images in Zelle graphics.py, tkinter can't read image data A:

To transform your presumed .gif into a reliable GIF, readable by "graphics.py" (Tkinter behind) or to convert from other formats (e.g. .jpg, etc), you can use:

macOS
sips -s format gif your-source-image.gif --out your-image.gif

Linux
convert your-source-image.gif your-image.gif

Windows (Powershell)
magick your-source-image.gif your-image.gif

This should be enough for the GIF part.

The JPG issue
(macOS proceeding; logic valid for other platforms [the crux is the bridge: pillow - "graphics.py"[Tkinter]]).
You will need a graphics.py version that knows how to talk with pillow, otherwise it won't work unless you tinker the former.
If you want your program to work with formats like .jpg leaning on graphics.py (Zelle's book ad hoc graphics library [wrapper]), you will need to install pillow. Apart from the standard brew install pillow (recommended), you can go for the local-installation/sandboxed choice (to avoid conflicts with your current Homebrew/native Python installation).
If you try: python3 -m pip install pillow, "error: externally-managed-environment" message will be triggered and you will be advised to do:

  1. python3 -m venv venv                Creates folder on working directory for the isolated environment
  2. source venv/bin/activate        Sources environment configuration
  3. pip install pillow                    Install pillow in the venv folder
  4. python3 your-script.py            Now your script should work properly

This will create an isolated environment apart from your system's Python wide installation. Usually with a shell prompt prefixed with: (venv) .... The only drawback is that you will need to source it again anytime you need it.
To uninstall pillow installed this way, type this inside the special shell:

  1. deactivate                 Prefix (venv) ... will dissapear
  2. rm -rf venv               Remove pillow's local installation folder

At any moment you can check the installation state with: brew info pillow

*Third, not recommended although nor dramatic, option: python3 -m pip install pillow --break-system-packages. Worst case you would need to re-install Python again, if relevant-for-you conflicts arise in the future with related packages.

If after installing pillow you still get: _tkinter.TclError: couldn't recognize data in image file "your-image.jpg", you probably need to tune graphics.py to import and use pillow functionalities (basically to deal with image formats [beyond Tkinter's .gif, .pgm, .ppm, .png] that pillow is capable and "graphics.py" (Tkinter) is not). Later versions of graphics.py should include pillow awareness. If not, tuning is possible and could require an import... and a couple of lines more in certain places inside graphics.py.

*Zelle's book is for you to learn Object-Oriented Programming, not for you to fight with macOS (or others) graphics drivers and Tkinter dependencies.

Q: execute javascript (node.js) code right from Visual Studio in REPL manner A:

  1. On Settings, change the Files: Auto Save config to afterDelay.

  2. On the Terminal panel open a new Bash or PowerShell tab and type:

    node --watch yourFile.js

You got a REPL from yourFile.js re-executing 1 second after every keystroke.

No need to manually save. No need for extensions.
